correctness.rationale: Reconstructed Euclid's bijection, including leg ordering, positive parameters, parity and gcd. Derived r=n(m-n) and its square-factor equivalence with both coprime factors individually square. Checked that the hypotenuse is (u²+v²)²+u⁴. Proved the parity-restricted lattice estimate by monotone column summation, then used odd-divisor Möbius inversion. Euler product of odd squarefree Möbius weights equals 8/pi²; polar area gives κ=2/pi² times the stated integral. Error is O(X^(1/4)log(2X)) without assuming a conjectural prime estimate. Verified exact finite equality between two enumeration implementations up to X=2,000,000; the computation is corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The primary full text of Robbins 2006 was read (both pages) and supplies fixed-inradius counting but no growing-hypotenuse sum or asymptotic. Targeted literature searches found no same or stronger statement; the closest Pythagorean finding concerns square PERIMETERS with fixed prime support, logically different. Omland and O'Loughlin full texts were not accessible, so an earlier unindexed version remains a declared risk, not certified absence.

value.rationale: The statistic is motivated by a classical square condition on the natural integer inradius of primitive Pythagorean triangles. Unlike fixed-radius multiplicities and finite excess tables, the result determines a quantitative rarity exponent and a new explicit geometric constant with a power-saving (relative) error: kappa X^(1/2)+O(X^(1/4)log X). The gcd parity and quartic hypotenuse geometry are structurally essential, not arbitrary parameter restrictions. It is a complete unconditional infinite-family asymptotic, not a re-enumeration of examples or a routine numerical improvement.
